subject: phoenix
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: phoenix with flame plumage, wings spread.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning a phoenix design with flame plumage and spread wings in a Genshin Impact art style, using the toon and glow kits from the SDK to get cel-shaded fur edges and fiery highlights, while keeping the proportions around 1.6m with a wide wingspan.

I'm sketching the skeleton: a hip root with spine chain up to the neck and head, a flame-feathered tail chain, wings built from shoulder joints out to wrist and tip for a spread pose, and leg chains ending in talons planted on the ground. Still working out joint coordinates and planning to use extrude for feather blades, decals for anime-style eyes, and gradient painting for the flame coloring.

Still defining the skeleton hierarchy...

Noting the beak color option, then designing a flameBlade helper using extrude with a teardrop outline to build fiery crest spikes on the head. Moving on to planning the wings next.

Defining wing chain names...

Still shaping feather outline orientation...

Defining flame color palette...

Adding glow to crest and tail-tip accents, then building the tail as a backward-curving chain with flame-like feather blades extruded along it, cycling through red, orange, and yellow colors.

Now I'm setting up the legs: defining hip-knee-foot chains with forward-bending knees for each side, naming the joints hip/knee/ankle, and planning talon spikes at the ankle tips.

Defining rod helper and torso sweep...

Placing decals for both eyes with mirrored offsets around the head center, then starting on the head geometry itself as a sphere positioned on the bone...

Now I'm figuring out the crest shape, planning a series of extruded blades along the top of the head with varying base points to create a rising flame-like effect.

Defining the outline type...

For the beak, I'm setting up a separate jaw joint parented to the head so the lower beak can move independently, with the upper beak fixed as a head spike and the lower beak as a jaw-bone spike. I'm positioning the eye decal relative to the head's radius and azimuth placement.

Now I'm working out the wing rig: shoulder joints parented to an upper spine joint, feather rows distributed along the wing chain using fractional positions, plus a separate trailing feather row along the wing.

I'm figuring out the feather plane orientation so blades trail back along -Z like fins, sweeping the wing tip radius from wider to narrower, naming the four wing joints, then moving into defining the body's cel-shaded paint and plumage colors.

Still writing color and limb setup...

Adding toe rods and talon spikes...

Wait, I need to check leg reach: hips at 0.92 height is too far from the ground foot position given a 0.64 total leg length, so I need to lower the hip height to around 0.55 with thigh and shank segments of about 0.22 each to make the geometry actually reach the ground.

That's a bit too long, so I'm adjusting leg lengths to [0.32,0.3] for a total reach of 0.62, keeping the hip-to-foot distance feasible with the hip at y 0.62 and target foot at y 0.03. Checking the lowest points overall—feet at ground level and tail position—to make sure nothing clips below zero.

Total height works out to roughly 1.95, which is reasonable for a phoenix figure of this scale, and the head sphere and neck joint positions line up correctly. Now I'm defining a blade function for the flame-shaped crest feathers, building an outline that tapers from a wide base to a sharp point and extruding it into a thin 3D shape, then planning to loop through several of these to build the crest along the top of the head.

Placing the crest blades around the back of the head with positions and directions that vary slightly per blade, leaning each one back and outward with normalized direction vectors so the crest fans out naturally, and tapering their lengths across the row.

Coloring each crest blade with alternating flame colors and adding a glow effect for emissive strength. Now moving to the tail feathers, setting up similar extruded blades that stick outward and down along the tail's backward direction with vertical blade orientation.

Adding more wing feathers...

I'm checking that chain.at(t) returns a frame-like point usable directly for extrude placement, confirming primary feathers get longer toward the wingtip. Now moving on to setting up the eyes.

For the head, I'm applying a gradient paint between red and yellow for the cel-shaded sphere, and working out the surface for placing eye hits around the head center—making sure I handle the case where the surface query returns null.

Now I'm drafting the full module, setting up imports from the agentic-3js-builder SDK (limb, gradient, countershade, cel, glow, animeEye, and toon/glow kits), then initializing the builder with a "phoenix" name before defining the spine sweep for radii.

Still shaping torso radii...

Head joint should parent off the second neck segment's end point so it follows the neck chain naturally. Now I'm starting to write the actual character-building code, importing the builder utilities, gradient, limb, and cel-shading helpers.

Still writing imports and helper functions...

Defining the head gradient and starting the spine joint hierarchy with a catmull-rom curve for positioning.

Adding head and jaw joints...

Now I'm adding the crest and tuft details, then setting up eye decals using a hit-based positioning system with iris color variants, calculating azimuth and elevation angles to place them correctly on the skull sphere, and starting on the beak geometry using spike shapes anchored to the head bone.

Still writing crest loop...

Building each wing chain...

Still defining feather orientation...

Still defining the tail chain...

Building the leg chain with hip, knee, and ankle joints, then adding three splayed toe points extending forward from each foot...

Checking the toe mirroring math works out fine, and deciding to skip extra thigh and belly feathers for budget reasons. I'm adding a yellow glow accent to the tail blade tips, and considering whether to add a gold collar accent for a Genshin-style look.

Skipping the gold torque for safety, I'm instead adding small glowing fire-wisp spheres at each wing tip using a warm gold-yellow color. Finishing up by returning the root and double-checking the plume geometry outline handles its sharp point correctly.
